# NOTES: The Induna's Wife (Bertram Mitford; Gutenberg #32927)
Single book. Narrated by Untuswa (old Zulu/Matabele induna) to "Nkose" (white listener) in a waggon at the old Kambula camp during a storm. Frame: Prologue, then Chapters 1–25.

## Frame (Prologue)
- Narrator (white, "I") at ruined Kambula Camp, drizzle, natives subdued, waggon leader eager to leave water-hole. Untuswa arrives out of the dark ("Nkose!"); narrator offers tywala, blanket, snuff. Ox with wide horns looks like a headless vast head; Untuswa mutters in wonder, then begins his story.

## Ch 1: The Tale of the Red Death
- Background: Untuswa defeated Dingane at Place of the Three Rifts; saved King Umzilikazi's life (won White Shield); married Lalusini (sorceress, full blood of House of Senzangakona, daughter of Tshaka; found among the Bakoni, "stamped flat").
- Umzilikazi (at Kwa'zingwenya) grows suspicious; asks Untuswa to name the man greater than kings "in this house." Untuswa deflects.
- Messengers from Maqandi-ka-Mahlu's iron-workers (region north, mountains, ghosts): men killed in Ghost/Red Death Valley by a ghost-bull (gored, ripped). Seer Gasitye entered; 20 bodies. Umzilikazi: send Untuswa's regiment of "Scorpions" to drive people into valley; slay ghost or be slain. Messenger pleads; Umzilikazi sneers.
- Izanusi (witch doctors) howl. Hlatusa (leader of 20-man party) reports 2 more killed; hoof-mark of huge bull. Umzilikazi sends Hlatusa to the Pool of the Alligators; Hlatusa walks to death.

## Ch 2: "Behold the Sign!"
- Thunder omen. People demand victim. Izanusi chief (Notalwa's predecessor reference; Notalwa and Isilwana earlier) names witch-queen Lalusini. Bakoni slaves confess the Red Death precedes succession of new chief; Lalusini and mother Laliwa caused Tauane's predecessor's death. Umzilikazi fears succession; plans to kill Untuswa, put Lalusini on high throne (stake).
- Slaves burned on hill; lightning. Lalusini before King: "In the hand of the King is death..." prophecy of House of Matyobane's ruin. Umzilikazi orders stake for her.
- Lalusini calls "Behold the sign!" lightning strikes burning pile, bones scattered; slayers stunned; her "sign" saves her.
- Umzilikazi gives Untuswa a condition: slay horror before full moon, alone, unarmed force; else Untuswa and house become alligator food and Lalusini gets stake.

## Ch 3: An Ominous Parting
- Untuswa's reflections on decline; Lalusini's appearance unchanging; no children by her. Untuswa plans revolt ("what has happened before can happen again"; Tshaka's death).
- Lalusini divines; gives impala-skin muti bag ("open only in extremity, when wit and wit of others fail"). Untuswa wears it on thong.
- Departure at sunset; Lalusini in doorway in sun's glow. Jambula (Xosa slave, captured from Basuti) with him. Lion; muti stops it.

## Ch 4: The Abode of the Terror
- Kraal of Maqandi (mist). Maqandi sullen, fearful. Untuswa dismisses armed attendants; 2 iron-worker slaves; slave Suru left alone at a rock (threatened with impalement). Night watch: ghost-bull rises above rocks; Suru screams and is killed. Hoofprints.

## Ch 5: Gasitye the Wizard
- Voice from cliff (old Masuka's voice, then Gasitye's mocking cackle); rock door opens. Gasitye's cave: green flame, fire in clay bowl. Visions of dead: Hlatusa, Tyuyumane, Notalwa, brother Sekweni, Gungana, Tauane, Nangeza. Untuswa stunned.

## Ch 6: The Ghost-Bull
- Untuswa wakes in open; Gasitye: "Dust—all dust!" Second slave dead. Jambula plan: lure bull under mimosa; Untuswa drops on back, drives assegai into spine. Head cut off. Moon nearly full (Jambula: "six days"). Untuswa had slept six days in cave.
- Jambula sent for ironworkers to carry trophies.

## Ch 7: The Faith of a King
- Crowd at Kwa'zingwenya; guard commander Ngoza. Umzilikazi: head stinks; mocks Untuswa's conditions (moon, unarmed force, Jambula). Untuswa's kraal; wives Nxope, Fumana say Lalusini disappeared 3rd night after he left. Untuswa threatens them with spear; resolves to slay King himself. Brother Mgwali, Ncala-cala (kraal head).

## Ch 8: Gegesa's Tale
- Untuswa takes new wife (daughter of induna Xulawayo, lobola paid). Umzilikazi jokes about women. Old witch Gegesa (said killed under Tshaka) tells: Lalusini thrown into the pool by four slayers (names given) on King's word. Untuswa throws Gegesa in river.
- Jambula, now trusted, plans murder.

## Ch 9: "To Slay Thee, Son of Matyobane"
- Night attack: two izinceku killed; Untuswa grapples Umzilikazi, shouts "Where is Lalusini?" Umzilikazi's wife flees and cries; guards come. Muti bag torn; stupefying scent knocks King out. Guards recognize King; Untuswa escapes over stockade. Flees, hunted.
- Mountain Inkume; mist; ledge; cave; Jambula found alive in cave.

## Ch 10: The Faith of a Slave
- Jambula warns of search parties; they flee to plains; pheebok doe and fawn spare them (vow never to kill that species). Jambula reports: Untuswa's kraal burned; people fled.
- Jambula captured by Sivuma (sub-chief) who tortures him with red-hot irons; Jambula leads to Untuswa's hiding but fights; hurls himself into river, dies.

## Ch 11: The Rumble of the Elephant
- Untuswa wanders two moons; goes to kraal of Nomapela (chief returning from Swazi raid); Mfulwana (scarred shoulder Untuswa inflicted at Three Rifts) recognizes him. Reach Nkunkundhlovu (Dingane's kraal, "Rumble of the Elephant"). Dingane (tall, leopard-skin chair) gives him three Swazi girls as wives; Umhlela, Tambusa (fierce, hates Untuswa), Nomapela, Mfulwana.

## Ch 12: A Devouring Swarm
- Untuswa tells Dingane he seeks revenge on House of Matyobane; Dingane intrigues. Silwane (Imbele-bele, formerly enemy) becomes friend. Untuswa's Swazi wife Nomshasa dreams of woman. Boers (Amabuna) invade; Dingane kills headmen. Missionary (Umfundisi) warns Dingane; Dingane's replies about God and torments; sends him away.

## Ch 13: The Tongue of the Snake
- Council: Tambusa opposes sending to Tegwini (Durban). Untuswa: "swarm of locusts stamped flat." Amabuna leaders come to talk land (between Tugela & Umzimvubu); Dingane: "two bulls cannot rule in one kraal"; they're sent to retake cattle from Sikonyela. Tambusa: "head of the snake, only its tongue."

## Ch 14: The Head of the Snake
- Amabuna return with cattle; song; mock charge. On third night secret council: Untuswa advises destroy camp and waylay returners. Amabuna come unarmed to Nkunkundhlovu; struck down by songs of "mouth of the white man" and killed by stick-wielders. Tambusa: "head of the snake is crushed." Narrator justifies Dingane's actions.

## Ch 15: The Crushing of the Snake
- Dingane's speech: "make an end of it utterly." Impi attacks waggon camp, slays women and children. Other camp: waggon fort, long guns, failed attack. Untuswa and Silwane lead charge; repulse with heavy losses. Cattle taken.

## Ch 16: Of a New Witch-Finding
- Dingane angry; Tambusa and Umhlela muster men. Witch doctor Tola (chief izanusi) plans "smelling out"; band of singing girls sings of "the stranger." Untuswa about to be named; Lalusini appears as "Mahlula" (girls obey her; she prophesies). Dingane orders Tola and izanusi killed (clubbed). Tambusa upset.

## Ch 17: The Dwelling of the Wise One
- Untuswa seeks Mahlula; message from girl: "Mahlula waits" at reed-beds. Lalusini in earth cave; reveals she leapt into the pool and escaped; Tambusa/Tola enmity. Lalusini advises caution. Untuswa's vengeance softens.
- Hyenas; woman's moan.

## Ch 18: The Refugees of the Ngome
- Nomshasa, the Swazi wife, found dying: tortured by Tambusa and Umhlela (their accusation from her dream-talk). Untuswa kills her with a knob-stick at her request. Silwane sings warning. Lalusini says: flee to Bapongqolo in Ngome forests.
- Untuswa in Ngome forests; refugees (Bapongqolo) seize him.

## Ch 19: The Vengeance of the Refugees
- Leader Sifadu, son of Kona (father eaten by black ants after Tola's naming). Untuswa joins. Lalusini meets Untuswa; Tola (apparently alive) captured by Untuswa; Sifadu punishes Tola by ant-nest hanging.

## Ch 20: The Bapongqolo Return
- Untuswa gains following; Sifadu challenges; Untuswa kills Sifadu (sword-leg slash). Untuswa elected chief of Bapongqolo. News: Dingane retreats; Nkunkundhlovu burnt. Bapongqolo march; song; kneel with weapons down; Dingane: "retreat" then encircle.

## Ch 21: The Embassy of Tambusa
- Dingane spares Bapongqolo; makes Untuswa induna. Mahlula vouches. Mpande (brother) defects to Amabuna; Nongalaza leads rebels. Tambusa sent as envoy; insulted with "Kafir," shot with Nkombazana.

## Ch 22: The Dividing of the Nation
- Dingane's speech: "lion-cubs of Zulu." Battle: Nongalaza's men switch; Umhlela killed; cry "Amabuna are at hand" (false) causes flight. Untuswa retreats to Ngome.

## Ch 23: A Hard Ordeal
- Lalusini (hard look) urges Untuswa to kill sleeping Dingane under rock; he refuses. Lalusini vanishes. Untuswa leads King to hidden caves in Lebombo. Dingane: "Untuswa, my friend."

## Ch 24: The Stroke of Sopuza
- Untuswa gathers army (Silwane, Nomapela, Bapongqolo). Dingane restored; Ngome kraal. Assassins (Amaswazi) stab Dingane; Untuswa kills one; Lalusini (as fugitive) is caught — "The stroke of Sopuza has fallen." Dingane dies after farewell speech to warriors.

## Ch 25: Conclusion
- Dingane buried secretly. Army accepts Mpande; Mpande's favor. Lalusini returns to Untuswa's hut; says she will live as an induna's wife. Narrator notes Anglo-Zulu background (Kambula/Ulundi) and reflects on morality of history. Untuswa sleeps under waggon.

## Key Names
Untuswa (son of Ntelani, Umtetwa); Lalusini/Mahlula; Umzilikazi (Matyobane's son); Dingane; Mpande; Tambusa; Umhlela; Silwane; Nomapela; Mfulwana; Tola; Sifadu; Jambula; Suru; Gasitye; Masuka; Hlatusa; Maqandi-ka-Mahlu; Nangeza; Fumana; Nxope; Nomshasa; Gegesa; Sivuma; Nongalaza; Nkombazana; Sodosi; Ngoza; Xulawayo; Kalipe; Mgwali; Ncala-cala; Tauane; Tyuyumane; Notalwa; Sikonyela; Sekweni; Kona.

## Places
Kwa'zingwenya; Nkunkundhlovu; Place of Three Rifts; Valley of Red Death; Inkume; Ngome forests; Lebombo; Imbele-bele; Tegwini (Durban); Mahlabatini plain; Nodwengu; Kambula.
